links.outcome: Segmentation Dice in cross-validation versus independent external single-institution validation
links.effect: Tumor core Dice 0.937 in cross-validation vs 0.872 externally with heterogeneous protocols and incomplete sequences; volume correlation r 0.995 vs 0.971.
links.quote: In external validation (310 cases, single institution), mean tumor core Dice was 0.872 despite heterogeneous MRI protocols and incomplete sequences; tumor core volume correlation remained strong (r = 0.971).

links.effect: Performance reported as equitable across demographic subgroups; most common failures were skull base and intraosseous tumors.
links.quote: Most common failure modes were skull base and intraosseous tumors with performance equitable across demographic subgroups.

links.outcome: Blinded radiologist Likert ratings of model segmentations versus reference annotations
links.effect: Model segmentations scored higher than reference annotations (+0.32 BraTS; +1.38 external validation), suggesting imperfect reference standards.
links.quote: In blinded evaluation (1120 ratings), model segmentations received higher scores than reference annotations (+0.32 BraTS; +1.38 external validation).

screen.reason: Evaluates a deep learning model for automated meningioma segmentation with external validation and a blinded reader study involving 10 radiologists assessing segmentation quality, failure modes, and equity, but does not test a specific deployment practice/guardrail.
